findings.detail: The updated doc says that with saved Autopilot consent, a controller can download catalog builds on the operator's behalf unless the operator opts out. Previously, 'downloads' were explicitly not authorized. The documented config table makes `max_storage_gb` and `max_models` default to absent (no cap), leaving only a 50 GiB free-disk reserve as a default guard. A compromised or misbehaving controller or coordinator could use `prefetch_model` to fill the model-cache volume, up to 50 GiB of free space remains. That degrades provider availability (T-016-style disk pressure) and widens the A-004 weights and TB-002 trust surface. Consent is the only gate, and consent was originally for model selection, not bulk downloads. Fix: default to bounded `max_storage_gb` and `max_models`, or require a separate explicit download opt-in. Update the threat model to cover controller-initiated downloads. The implementing code is not in this doc-only diff, so the behavior is unverified.
findings.title: Autopilot downloads become default-on for consented Macs with no default storage or model cap

findings.detail: model-autopilot.md head lines 5-10 and the new sections (~37-130) reverse the base statement (base lines 5-7) that consent does not authorize downloads. A saved opt-in now exposes every verified cached catalog build and permits coordinator-initiated downloads by default. The doc also says neither change bumps the consent `revision`. An operator who consented under the old meaning ('explicitly consented cached models') therefore gains download and set-widening authority without re-consent. The coordinator is trusted, so this is not an adversarial bypass. It does create new provider-side attack surface that no threat-model entry covers: coordinator-driven disk consumption (50 GiB reserve, no default storage cap; related to T-016); fetching and publishing catalog weights (A-004/T-012/T-027 weight-hash verification); and the owner-only `autopilot-downloads.json` ledger. Fix: add a threat-model entry or TB covering Autopilot downloads, set widening, the ledger and placement holds. Also consider requiring a consent revision or explicit re-consent before enabling downloads by default for pre-existing consent records.
findings.title: Existing Autopilot consent now silently authorizes default-on downloads and a wider model set, with no threat-model coverage

findings.detail: The BASE architecture limits Autopilot to explicitly consented cached models and excludes download authority. The new contract enables downloads whenever consent is already saved, with no storage/model cap by default (lines 86–100). It also expands the controllable set without a prompt or consent revision change (lines 39–45 and 70–75). Thus an operator who approved only cached builds can have controller-directed transfers consume bandwidth and disk and introduce additional controllable models without approving the expanded authority. The CLI patch confirms that saved enrollment now automatically includes these builds. Preserve the old scope for existing consent records: require an explicit, versioned opt-in for downloads and automatic inventory expansion, or default those capabilities off until renewed consent. Document this expanded operator/resource-control boundary in the threat model.
findings.title: Existing cached-model consent now authorizes default-on downloads without renewed consent
